title: Domed end cap for M8 threaded rod
prompt: Domed cap to cover the sharp end of an M8 threaded rod (my bed frame has a few sticking out). 14 mm outside diameter: a 10 mm tall straight section with a full hemispherical dome on top, so 17 mm tall overall. In the bottom there's an 8.4 mm hole, 12 mm deep, so it slides over the rod; I'll glue it on.

hidden_tests.description: Evaluates cleanly and every body is a valid closed solid
Exactly one solid body (one printable part)
14 mm diameter, 17 mm tall overall, ±0.1 mm
The top is one spherical face (a true hemisphere, not a cone or a flat top)
Two cylindrical faces: the outside and the rod hole
Two flat faces: the bottom ring and the end of the blind hole
Volume π·7²·10 + ⅔π·7³ − π·4.2²·12 ≈ 1592.7 mm³ ±1% (catches an 8.0 hole or a wrong depth)

notes: M8 clearance 8.4 (ISO 273 medium). A 12 mm deep hole leaves 5 mm of material above it on the axis.
